reluctant.headline: Man reluctant to enter the building
story: Tom arrived at the office just before the meeting.
He stopped near the glass door and looked inside.
His team waved, but he kept stepping back.
Tom was reluctant to enter the room.
A friend said Tom is often reluctant when many people are watching.
reluctant.question: Why did Tom wait?

answers.text: He did not really want to enter

reluctant.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Reluctant means he did not really want to do it.
reluctant.feedbackIncorrect: Almost. Reluctant means he did not really want to do it.

reluctant.headline: Student reluctant to answer
story: Sara looked at the question on the board.
She knew part of the answer and held her pen tightly.
The room became quiet while everyone waited.
Sara was reluctant to answer in front of the class.
Her teacher smiled because Sara still looked reluctant, not confused.
reluctant.question: How did Sara feel?

answers.text: Unsure and not ready to answer

reluctant.feedbackCorrect: Correct. She was not eager to answer.
reluctant.feedbackIncorrect: Almost. She was not eager to answer.

reluctant.headline: Player reluctant to join the match
story: Mike stood beside the field after the break.
His team needed one more player and called his name.
He looked at his sore leg and did not move.
Mike was reluctant to join the match.
Even when the coach waved, Mike still seemed reluctant to play.
reluctant.question: What does reluctant mean here?

answers.text: He did not really want to join

reluctant.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Reluctant means not really wanting to do something.
reluctant.feedbackIncorrect: Almost. Reluctant means not really wanting to do something.
